- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day window; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the first 5–7 days.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+ → 72+), then overshoots and fails to capture subsequent mean reversion; reduce forecast by 2–5% after spike peaks.
- Underestimates in late period (last 7–10 days) — model lags behind true trend; increase forecast by 1–4% for final 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model holds too low for extended periods; apply upward bias of 0.5–2% per day for 3–5 days after price dips.
- Forecast tends to be too conservative in mid-period (days 8–15) — adjust upward by 1–3% for days 10–15 if history shows upward momentum.
- Avoid overfitting to recent low prices — if last 5 days are below 65, don’t assume trend continues; add 2–5% buffer to avoid underestimating rebound.
